verdicts.threatModel: A compromised or unexpectedly changed Google release-list response can select a different archive at the allowed host.
verdicts.reachability: installChromeForTesting consumes mutable channel metadata, downloads its selected URL, extracts it, and records a digest after download.
verdicts.impact: QA tooling can execute an unpinned Chrome archive; recorded digest is evidence, not an authenticity check.
verdicts.devilsAdvocate: Host allowlisting, HTTPS, archive extraction shape, and executable existence checks reduce accidental misrouting but do not bind bytes to an expected digest.

verdicts.threatModel: A binary download is unsafe only when no independent integrity pin exists.
verdicts.reachability: The candidate URL is an archive descriptor, but its adjacent sha256 field is consumed as the archive pin.
verdicts.impact: No unpinned model artifact is established by this line.
verdicts.devilsAdvocate: This adjudication covers adjacent source only; runtime verification remains outside this bounded review.

verdicts.threatModel: A remote model file without an expected digest could be replaced.
verdicts.reachability: The URL is paired with sha256 and size fields in the same RemoteFile descriptor.
verdicts.impact: Scanner URL match does not show missing integrity metadata.
verdicts.devilsAdvocate: This does not prove every installer path enforces the descriptor; it closes only this candidate.

verdicts.threatModel: A repinning tool could publish a URL without binding downloaded bytes.
verdicts.reachability: repin downloads the exact release asset, hashes it, and writes both URI and expected SHA-256 into bootstrap.
verdicts.impact: The flagged URI is an input to a digest-pinning workflow, not an unverified installer fetch.
verdicts.devilsAdvocate: The release tag itself is mutable in principle; the generated bootstrap's expected hash remains the byte-level check.

verdicts.threatModel: Binary pinning rules apply to executable or model artifact downloads.
verdicts.reachability: The URL is documentation for Pinterest OAuth setup.
verdicts.impact: No artifact download or execution follows this line.
verdicts.devilsAdvocate: OAuth endpoint security needs separate protocol review; this binary-pin candidate does not establish it.

verdicts.threatModel: Binary pinning rules apply to executable or model artifact downloads.
verdicts.reachability: The URL configures an OpenAI-compatible API base URL.
verdicts.impact: No local binary is fetched from this endpoint.
verdicts.devilsAdvocate: Remote API trust is a separate data-safety/security concern, outside this scanner rule.

verdicts.threatModel: Binary pinning rules apply to artifact consumers, not release metadata links.
verdicts.reachability: The URL is emitted as a GitHub release manifest link after publication artifacts are already sealed and hashed.
verdicts.impact: This line does not fetch or install the manifest.
verdicts.devilsAdvocate: Downstream consumers still need manifest verification; that is governed by their own adoption checks.

verdicts.threatModel: A model artifact URL should be adjudicated where bytes are fetched or verified.
verdicts.reachability: The candidate is a shared model-worker base URL used to compose platform-specific routes; no artifact is fetched at this declaration.
verdicts.impact: Base endpoint declaration alone does not prove an unpinned binary path.
verdicts.devilsAdvocate: Composed routes require separate per-artifact pin review; this bounded verdict does not close those candidates.

coverage.reason: Packet had candidate-verdict coverage only and no source excerpts; full adjudication would require source review for every candidate.

details.method: Reviewed representative source-backed candidates across binary-pins, model descriptors, release tooling, API configuration, and release metadata. No generic dismissal was assigned to unreviewed candidates.
